user_story.role: developer with a JSON file open
user_story.capability: a one-click way to visualize it from the editor itself
user_story.benefit: I don't have to leave VS Code or use an external tool

criteria.trigger: the active editor's language is JSON or JSONC
criteria.behavior: display a "Visualize JSON" control in the editor title area

criteria.trigger: the active editor's language is not JSON or JSONC
criteria.behavior: keep the "Visualize JSON" control hidden

criteria.trigger: a developer activates the "Visualize JSON" control
criteria.behavior: open a visualization panel beside the source editor
open the visualization panel alongside the source editor without replacing it as the default editor for `.json`/`.jsonc` files

user_story.capability: the extension to read the exact contents of my file and tell me clearly if it can't be parsed
user_story.benefit: the visualization never shows stale or misleading data

criteria.trigger: a visualization panel opens for a document
criteria.behavior: parse the document's current full text into a structured view model

criteria.trigger: the document's text is not valid JSON (or JSONC per its own comment/trailing-comma rules)
criteria.behavior: produce an error view model containing the parse error's message and location, instead of a partial or crashed result

criteria.trigger: the View_Model_Builder produces an error view model
criteria.behavior: display the parse error inline in the panel instead of a blank or crashed panel

user_story.capability: to browse the JSON as a collapsible tree
user_story.benefit: I can drill into nested structures at my own pace

criteria.trigger: the Tree view mode is active
criteria.behavior: display each JSON object and array as a collapsible node showing its key/index and child count

criteria.trigger: the Tree view mode is active
criteria.behavior: auto-expand every node at nesting depth less than 2

criteria.trigger: the Tree view mode is active
criteria.behavior: leave every node at nesting depth 2 or greater collapsed by default

criteria.trigger: a developer clicks a node's chevron
criteria.behavior: toggle that node's own expanded/collapsed state without changing any sibling node's state

criteria.trigger: a developer activates the "expand all" control
criteria.behavior: expand every node in the Tree view

criteria.trigger: a developer activates the "collapse all" control
criteria.behavior: collapse every node in the Tree view

criteria.trigger: the Tree view mode is active
criteria.behavior: color-code null, boolean, number, and string leaf values by type, using the active VS Code color theme's variables

user_story.capability: a Finder-style drill-down through nested objects and arrays
user_story.benefit: I can inspect one branch of a large structure without the rest of the tree scrolling out of view

criteria.trigger: the Column view mode is active
criteria.behavior: display each level of the currently drilled-down path as its own column of entries

criteria.trigger: a developer selects an object or array entry in a column
criteria.behavior: open a new column to its right showing that entry's children

criteria.trigger: a developer selects a scalar entry in a column
criteria.behavior: show that value in a detail pane instead of opening a new column

criteria.trigger: a developer drags a column's resize handle
criteria.behavior: adjust that column's width accordingly

user_story.capability: plain objects and arrays of similar objects rendered as tables
user_story.benefit: I can scan many records or fields at a glance like a spreadsheet

criteria.trigger: the Key-Value/Table view mode is active and the current node is a JSON object
criteria.behavior: display its keys and values as rows of a table

criteria.trigger: the Key-Value/Table view mode is active and the current node is an array of objects
criteria.behavior: display the array as a grid with one row per array element

criteria.trigger: the Key-Value/Table view mode is active
criteria.behavior: show a preview badge indicating type and size for any cell whose value is itself an object or array, rather than the full nested content

user_story.capability: to switch freely between Tree, Column, and Table
user_story.benefit: I can pick whichever fits what I'm looking for at the moment

criteria.trigger: a developer selects a different view mode from the panel's toggle
criteria.behavior: re-render the same underlying view model in the newly selected mode

criteria.trigger: a developer opens the first visualization panel of a VS Code installation
criteria.behavior: default to Tree view mode

criteria.trigger: a developer opens any subsequent visualization panel
criteria.behavior: default to the view mode most recently selected in that VS Code installation

user_story.capability: the visualization to match my VS Code color theme
user_story.benefit: it looks native rather than clashing with my editor

criteria.behavior: style all panel content using VS Code's active color theme's CSS variables

criteria.trigger: the developer switches VS Code's active color theme while a panel is open
criteria.behavior: update the panel's colors to match the new theme without the panel being closed and reopened

user_story.capability: the visualization to stay in sync with the file
user_story.benefit: I don't have to close and reopen the panel after every edit

criteria.trigger: the visualized document's text changes while its panel is open
criteria.behavior: parse the document's updated full text into a new view model

criteria.trigger: the View_Model_Builder produces a new view model for a document whose panel is open
criteria.behavior: send that view model to the panel

criteria.trigger: the Renderer receives an updated view model for the document currently shown
criteria.behavior: re-render the active view mode with the new data

criteria.trigger: the document associated with an open visualization panel is closed
criteria.behavior: stop sending further updates for that panel

criteria.trigger: the document's updated text is not valid JSON
criteria.behavior: display the parse error inline instead of the previous valid rendering

user_story.capability: to be certain that browsing the visualization can never change my file
user_story.benefit: I can use it without worrying about accidental edits

criteria.behavior: render every JSON value as non-editable content

criteria.trigger: a developer clicks or otherwise interacts with a value shown in the panel
criteria.behavior: leave the visualized document's text unchanged

criteria.trigger: the extension is packaged with the standard VS Code packaging tool
criteria.behavior: produce an installable `.vsix` file without requiring a configured Marketplace publisher account

criteria.trigger: the packaged `.vsix` is installed into a VS Code instance
criteria.behavior: behave identically to running the extension from the Extension Development Host
